title: Elgar, Cello Concerto, finale, in two recordings
work: Cello Concerto in E minor, Op. 85 — a shared passage from the finale
question: How sharply should the cello bite into the finale’s march?
intro: At Hayes on 22 December 1919, Beatrice Harrison recorded Elgar’s finale with the composer conducting. The whole concerto was recorded on four shellac sides. Beside Skidmore’s complete finale, this short passage is the point at which the cello joins the march, marked risoluto — resolute.

recordings.label: Beatrice Harrison and Edward Elgar, 1919
recordings.note: Harrison made the concerto’s first recording with Elgar conducting; their finale fitted on a single shellac side.

recordings.label: Skidmore College Orchestra
recordings.note: Skidmore plays the finale complete, including the cello’s late lament and the return of the concerto’s opening.

passages.label: Solo entry with the march theme
passages.note: The soloist takes up the brisk tune, marked risoluto. The tune is set with accents and short rests.

passages.label: Crescendo to accented high notes
passages.note: The cello rises through a crescendo to sharply accented high notes. The orchestra plays while the soloist rests.

passages.label: Solo and orchestra alternate
passages.note: Short solo phrases alternate with orchestral replies. The cello’s running notes carry the march forward between its clipped accents.

alignment.timeBasis: Absolute seconds in each supplied stream; trim ends are exclusive.

maps.scope: Continuous early-finale overlap only. Excludes Skidmore’s opening introduction, all earlier Harrison movements and all later cuts.
maps.inspection: The shared passage runs continuously through the early finale. Both performances play the same music here; the excerpts end before the later cuts.
